note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), bundled as library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz and read offline (owb-am). Every Scripture quotation was re-quoted to it verbatim (founder decision, 2026-11-18: Amharic quotes OWB everywhere), replacing the 1962/2003 UBS wording, the wording borrowed from other Amharic works, and the self-rendered Old Testament verses the first edition carried. Rows now carry chapter_order with a per-chapter block_index (the first edition counted blocks work-wide).

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: a span of the verse, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…' (Jer 2:6, Jer 31:21, Rom 3:10-12, Song 5:8, Matt 21:28-29); OWB's inner quotation marks become ‹› inside the book's «» (Gal 3:10, Luke 17:10, Isa 62:11). Bunyan's verbatim recitations without marks are quotations too (Rom 6:23, Rom 8:37, Ps 23:4, Ps 116:4, 2 Cor 4:18, 2 Cor 10:18, Mark 8:35, Prov 14:10, Prov 11:24 and 13:7, Eccl 10:3). Where the young-reader editions quote the same verse, the span is theirs (Ps 23:4, Jer 31:21, Isa 43:2, Acts 16:30's 'what must I do to be saved').

Where OWB's words force it, the sentence bends minimally: 'all that cometh is vanity' (Eccl 11:8) is OWB's እስትንፋስ with a one-time gloss (ማለትም ከንቱ ነው); the Valley of the Shadow of Death stays the allegory's place-name while Ps 23:4, Amos 5:8 and Job 12:22 give OWB's ድቅድቅ ጨለማ; 1 Cor 5:10 was cited 4:10 in the first edition (the English prints 5:10) and the citation is corrected; Isa 7:15 is OWB's ርጎና ማር beside the dish of ቅቤና ማር. Eccl 10:3 (ch10) opens a quotation mark the first edition never closes; that is left as it was.

A `self_rendered` row is one of Bunyan's margin references to an allusion or to his own paraphrase (most of the book's citations), or a quotation he adapts (person, tense, a token spoken to the pilgrim) or argues from in the AV's wording where OWB cannot carry it (Gen 13:13 'before the Lord', Prov 19:27, Prov 30:28's spider, Rev 22:14's 'do his commandments', Eccl 12:6's tokens); the reason is in `why`. The Japanese re-quote (#9898) made the same calls. Translations of this book are ai_unreviewed until a reviewer approves them.
